I am 68 years old and have farmed these 2 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. I never went to school, but the land has been my teacher. It is the start of spring, and my winter wheat is greening up after the cold months. Last autumn I sowed an improved wheat variety, and now I must take care of it until harvest in June. I will spread fertilizer when the soil warms — about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu, along with phosphate and potash. I have a well, and I will irrigate twice: once when the wheat starts jointing, and again when the grain is filling. If aphids show up, I will spray once. I do not plough deep like I used to; my back cannot take it, so I rely on rotary tillage. I expect around 450 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather is kind.

After I harvest the wheat in June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize right into the wheat stubble without tilling — my old bones cannot turn the soil twice in one week, and summer is short. I will apply fertilizer at planting and side-dress when the stalks are knee-high — about 13 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, plus some phosphorus and potassium. The maize will need one good irrigation from my well, maybe two if the rains fail. I will spray twice: first for weeds, and then for the corn borer. I hope to harvest around 500 kg per mu in the autumn. I keep my methods simple because I work this land alone, and at my age, simple and reliable is the only way.
